title: FormLogic Desktop plugin manifest
description: manifest.json at the root of a FormLogic Desktop plugin directory (e.g. plugins/aokie/manifest.json). Canonical copy: formlogic-app/docs/contracts/. schemaVersion 2 adds the additive ui/services/commands/data sections; schemaVersion 3 adds serviceDefinitions (SRV-402); schemaVersion 4 adds modules, agentTools and setup (OAIY's module system), and hosts that read it enforce minDesktopVersion. A section is refused under an older schemaVersion rather than half-honoured — a host that predates it would silently ignore the section, and a plugin that believes it declared something it did not is worse than one that fails to load.

allOf.description: schemaVersion 4 sections are refused under schemaVersion 1-3.

id.description: Stable plugin id. Also the default connector namespace.

pluginApiVersion.description: JSON-RPC protocol version the plugin speaks. Desktop refuses to start a plugin with a version it does not support.

minDesktopVersion.description: The oldest desktop that can run this plugin (semver). A host that reads schemaVersion 4 refuses the plugin, with a reason, when this is strictly greater than its own version; a value it cannot parse is a warning, not a refusal.

command.description: Executable path RELATIVE to the plugin directory. Absolute paths, drive letters and '..' segments are rejected by the loader.

capabilities.description: Permission strings the plugin's commands map to, e.g. "connector.aokie.call.answer". Desktop denies connector commands not covered by a declared capability.

events.description: Event names this plugin may emit. Desktop drops events whose name is not declared here.

ui.description: schemaVersion 2 — declarative UI contributions (PLG-203). Presentation-only: forward-compatible (unknown fields tolerated by the host). A bad entry is dropped with a warning; the manifest still loads.

screen.description: The ui.screens id this page shows.

section.description: Where the page goes. Absent: a sidebar section of its own (in `group`). A built-in section id (agent, flows, calendar, engines, services, connections, settings): a tab after that section's own tabs. One of this plugin's ui.sections ids: a tab of that section. Built-in sections can be extended, not replaced.

module.description: The page is shown only while this module is on.

sections.description: A plugin's own sidebar sections, whose tabs are the ui.nav pages naming them. A section no page names is dropped with a warning.

module.description: The section is shown only while this module is on.
The card is shown only while this module is on.

nav.description: A tile: the ui.nav id a click opens.

bind.description: The card's texts by name (headline, body, value, detail, ...). Each is text, or a binding the host looks up (paths only, never evaluated): $health.<status|detail|components>[.<path>] from the plugin's last health report, or $poll.<ui.statusCards id>.<path> from that card's last poll (polled no more often than every 5 s, only while the window is visible).

command.description: A declared connector command that is not journalled; sent with no payload.

services.description: schemaVersion 2 — plugin-owned service templates (PLG-206), installed with the plugin.

templateFile.description: Package-relative ServiceTemplate JSON path (no '..', no absolute).

serviceDefinitions.description: schemaVersion 3 — v3 Service Definitions this plugin contributes (SRV-402). Distinct from "services": those are legacy ServiceTemplates the desktop supervises as processes; these are catalog entries whose actions a flow can invoke. The host stamps each contributed definition with its provider (the plugin id), overwriting any provider the file claims, so a definition cannot fake provenance. Ids must be the plugin id or start with "<plugin-id>.", built-ins can never be shadowed, and one plugin owns an id.

definitionFile.description: Package-relative Service Definition v3 JSON path (no '..', no absolute).

journalled.description: Commands requiring a durable requestId (physical side effects). Each must be a declared connector command.

data.description: schemaVersion 2 — data the plugin stores OUTSIDE the desktop tree (shown on purge, never auto-deleted).

modules.description: schemaVersion 4 — the built-in modules this plugin provides: {"provides": [...]} or just the list. A module is on while a plugin providing it loads and is not turned off. A phone claim needs a connector declaring phone.status, sms.send, settings.get, settings.set and call.dial (the named `connector`, when given). Without this section, the plugin id `aokie` provides phone and calendar (the legacy rule).

connector.description: One of this plugin's connectors: the one serving the phone.

agentTools.description: schemaVersion 4 — this plugin's own service-definition actions offered to the agent as tools. The host takes the tool's description and input schema from the action and runs it through the gated service-action route (capability check, journalling, idempotency key).

action.description: <service definition id>/<action id>: an action of one of this plugin's serviceDefinitions.

name.description: What the agent calls it; unique within the plugin.

description.description: Instead of the action's own description.

audience.description: Where the tool is offered: the project conversation, the Front desk's runner, or its sms/call/task sessions. Default ["project"].

confirm.description: What the person approves before it runs, with {inputKey} placeholders, e.g. "Call {number}". Required when the action's sideEffects is not "none" (the entry is refused otherwise). Such a tool is refused in autonomous sessions (runner, sms, call, task) unless its audience lists them.

setup.description: schemaVersion 4 — this plugin's setup wizard, run by the host. The host always shows a permissions step first. A plugin needs setup while its setup.version is greater than the version its wizard last finished at.

when.description: The step is shown only while this check passes.

requires.description: requirements: what the plugin needs on this computer. There is no model id: an engineModel requirement is met by the model the person chose in Engines for that group.

fields.description: settings: the fields shown, read and written through the plugin's connector.

read.description: settings: default {"command": "settings.get", "path": "settings"}. A declared command that is not journalled.

write.description: settings: default {"command": "settings.set"}, sent {"<key>": value, ...}. A declared command.

screen.description: screen: a ui.screens id, shown in setup mode.

done.description: screen: the step is done while this check passes.

action.description: host: one of the host's own steps (phone.answerWithOaiy, calendar.business today). An action the host does not know is dropped with a warning, not a load failure.

check.description: A check: a command of one of this plugin's connectors that is not journalled, always sent with no payload, and a test of its answer. A command that errors, or takes more than 5 s, fails the check.

condition.description: A dot-separated path and exactly one operator. A missing path equals null.

present.description: The path exists and is not null.
